# CParser

`CParser` is a standalone C parser library written in C++, that can be easily embedded in other software projects. The library is contained of reusable set of classes.

## Demo usage of the library
See `src/cformat.cpp`, `include/GenCVisitor.h` and `src/GenCVisitor.cpp` for the demo source which uses the C parser library. `cformat` is an implementation of a simple C code style formatter.
To clone the project and build the demo, type:
```
$ git clone https://github.com/jkolek/cparser.git
$ cd cparser
$ make
```
To run the demo with example C file, type:
```
$ ./cformat test/example1.c
```

## How to use the library

To use the library you can simply implement your own visitor class by inheriting `TreeVisitor` class similarly like `GenCVisitor` (used by the `cformat`) does. Then with this visitor you can traverse abstract syntax tree generated by parser.

## Cephyr embedding changes

Cephyr feeds the lexer in-memory preprocessed C. An installed per-instance
diagnostic callback receives lexing, parsing, and semantic diagnostics without
redirecting process streams. A fatal diagnostic stops the translation unit;
the parser owns incomplete as well as successful ASTs. A nesting limit bounds
recursive grammar calls.

The integration preserves RV64 LP64 integer widths/ranks, literal spellings,
declaration storage flags, typedef scopes, parameter names and function
prototype/variadic information. `CompoundStmtASTNode::getItems()` is the
source-ordered view used for lowering. Named array declarators retain bounds
outermost-first; the AST represents `_Static_assert` without evaluating it.
Generic selections retain the controller and each ordered type/default
association, and designated initializers retain their ordered member/index
paths and nested initializer lists. C11 `u8` string tokens concatenate with
ordinary string tokens, and universal character names in strings decode as
UTF-8. In identifiers, direct UTF-8 and universal character names are checked
against C11 Annex D and use the same UTF-8 representation for name lookup.

This is not a complete C11 front end or ABI checker. Unsupported productions
include general enum initializer expressions, wide literals,
atomic and thread-local declarations, GNU attributes, and inline
assembly. The native lowerer has additional restrictions independent of the
syntax accepted here, including ASCII-only file-scope object and function
names.
See `cornerstone/Cephyr/tests/parser.cpp` for AST and diagnostic regressions.
